html:
Uto-Aztecan is a family of more than thirty Native American languages spoken from Oregon and Idaho to Mexico and Central America. Its name joins the Ute and the Aztecs, its two ends.

Its main branches:

  • Numic, of the Great Basin, spoken by the Western Shoshone, Southern Paiute and Ute. The Comanche carried it onto the southern plains.
  • Hopi, of the Hopi mesas.
  • Takic, of southern California, spoken by the Acjachemen and Cahuilla.
  • Southern languages of northwest Mexico, such as Yaqui and Huichol.
  • Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs, still spoken by over a million people.

The family probably split up 4,000 to 5,000 years ago. Its homeland, in the Southwest or in Mesoamerica, is debated.
